From c2626b7387210cff741be9fb91d317f02a70347c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Matthew Auld <matthew.auld@intel.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Feb 2024 15:31:11 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/xe/display: fix i915_gem_object_is_shmem() wrapper
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

shmem ensures the memory is cleared on allocation, however here we are
using TTM, which doesn't natively support shmem (other than for swap),
but instead just allocates normal system memory. And we only zero such
memory for userspace allocations. In the case of intel_fbdev we are
missing the memset_io() since display path incorrectly thinks object is
shmem based.

Fixes: 44e694958b95 ("drm/xe/display: Implement display support")
Signed-off-by: Matthew Auld <matthew.auld@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Suraj Kandpal <suraj.kandpal@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240205153110.38340-2-matthew.auld@intel.com
(cherry picked from commit 63fb531fbfda81bda652546a39333b565aea324d)
Signed-off-by: Thomas Hellström <thomas.hellstrom@linux.intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/compat-i915-headers/gem/i915_gem_object.h b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/compat-i915-headers/gem/i915_gem_object.h
index 68d9f6116bdf..777c20ceabab 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/compat-i915-headers/gem/i915_gem_object.h
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/compat-i915-headers/gem/i915_gem_object.h
@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@
 
 #include "xe_bo.h"
 
-#define i915_gem_object_is_shmem(obj) ((obj)->flags & XE_BO_CREATE_SYSTEM_BIT)
+#define i915_gem_object_is_shmem(obj) (0) /* We don't use shmem */
 
 static inline dma_addr_t i915_gem_object_get_dma_address(const struct xe_bo *bo, pgoff_t n)
 {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/xe/compat-i915-headers/gem/i915_gem_object.h`**
   - The macro definition for `i915_gem_object_is_shmem(obj)` was modified. 
   - The original definition checked if the object's flags included `XE_BO_CREATE_SYSTEM_BIT`, indicating it was a shared memory object.
   - The new definition simply returns `0`, indicating that the system does not use shared memory (`shmem`).

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change in the macro `i915_gem_object_is_shmem()` is aimed at correcting the behavior in the display path of the Intel framebuffer driver. The previous implementation incorrectly assumed that certain objects were shared memory, which led to missing memory initialization (specifically, the `memset_io()` function). By redefining the macro to always return `0`, the patch ensures that the display path does not mistakenly treat objects as shared memory, thus preventing potential issues related to uninitialized memory. This modification is part of a broader fix for a bug introduced in a previous commit related to display support.

drm/xe/display: fix i915_gem_object_is_shmem() wrapper
MIME-Version: 1.0

shmem ensures the memory is cleared on allocation, however here we are
using TTM, which doesn't natively support shmem (other than for swap),
but instead just allocates normal system memory. And we only zero such
memory for userspace allocations. In the case of intel_fbdev we are
missing the memset_io() since display path incorrectly thinks object is
shmem based.

Fixes: 44e694958b95 ("drm/xe/display: Implement display support")
Signed-off-by: Matthew Auld <matthew.auld@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Suraj Kandpal <suraj.kandpal@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240205153110.38340-2-matthew.auld@intel.com

Signed-off-by: Thomas Hellström <thomas.hellstrom@linux.intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect assumption in the display path that certain objects were shared memory (shmem) based, leading to a failure to properly initialize memory (missing `memset_io()`). This occurred because the macro `i915_gem_object_is_shmem()` was incorrectly defined to check for a flag that indicated shared memory usage, which was not applicable in the context of TTM memory allocation.

 #include "xe_bo.h"

+#define i915_gem_object_is_shmem(obj) (0) /* We don't use shmem */

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define i915_gem_object_is_shmem(obj) ((obj)->flags & XE_BO_CREATE_SYSTEM_BIT)
```
```c
// Missing memset_io() for non-shmem objects
```
Reason:
The macro `i915_gem_object_is_shmem()` incorrectly checks for a flag that indicates shared memory usage, which is not applicable for TTM memory allocation. This leads to the assumption that certain objects are shmem-based, resulting in the failure to initialize memory properly (missing `memset_io()`).

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define i915_gem_object_is_shmem(obj) (0) /* We don't use shmem */
```
Reason:
By redefining the macro to always return `0`, it correctly indicates that the objects are not shmem-based, preventing the incorrect assumption in the display path and ensuring that the necessary memory initialization (like `memset_io()`) is performed for TTM allocated memory.
